checks: No eclipse at 14 of 48 covered epochs where the 1.77049 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 257923571 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.770493 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.94 percent, while a secondary eclipse was not detected. The signal registers a detection significance of 199.7 in the box-least-squares search, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise of 15.8, though the centroid offset of 3.7 arcseconds from the target warrants further investigation. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. One notable feature of the data is a significant alternating pattern in eclipse depths, suggesting the initially measured period was half the true orbital period. Pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing remain consistent with this corrected period of 1.770493 days.
